title: Functions: triggers and bindings, and why bindings are the point

videos.script: A function in Azure is easy to picture as a piece of code that Azure calls on its own. {{app}} What Azure runs is a function app: Microsoft's host program, with your code loaded into it. This lesson builds one for the shop, from four short files, and runs it on your laptop. The image is Microsoft's own, and Azurite stands in for the storage account. {{http}} The first function takes an order over HTTP. You will break it, and see what the caller gets back. {{queue}} Then the order goes on a queue, and a second function picks it up. You will send an order the shop cannot price, and watch the host try it five times. After the fifth, it moves the message to a poison queue. {{bindings}} None of that is in your code. Two decorators asked the host for it, and they are called bindings. You will read what they wrote, and then take away the bundle they come from. {{azure}} Last, what changes in Azure: the plan that hosts the app, and connections made with an identity instead of a key.
